prompt:
Image 1 is the pose and layout guide: four grey clay maquettes of this giant in a 2 by 2 grid, one action in each cell, rendered from the game's battle camera. Copy from it exactly, cell by cell, the camera angle, the direction the body faces, the pose, the figure's size and its place in the cell. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified round shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the body, its anatomy and every detail follow Image 2.
Image 2 is the approved painted game cutout of this exact giant, standing at rest, seen from the same camera in the same view. Paint the same individual, with exactly the same head, shapes, proportions, colours, materials, markings and equipment, in the same painting style and the same light, now in the actions of Image 1. It must be unmistakably the same giant in all four cells.

One sheet: four painted figures of the same giant, full body, one in each cell of a 2 by 2 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF) background, as game cutouts. Read left to right, top row first:
Top left: struck and staggering: leaning back, the head thrown back, both arms flung out to the sides, the club still held, one foot stepping back.
Top right: dead: fallen flat on its back on the ground, the arms flung out, the club fallen beside it, its head toward the lower left of the image (it fell backwards, toward us).
Bottom left: the follow-through: the club carried on past the body low to its left after the blow, the body twisted far round to the left.
Bottom right: falling: buckling forward onto one knee, the head bowed, the club sagging toward the ground.
Every cell takes its pose from Image 1, never from Image 2: Image 2 shows only what the giant looks like, and its standing pose must not be copied into any cell. Each pose is strong and unmistakable at a glance.

Camera: high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The giant faces away from us, toward the upper right of the image, as in Image 1 and Image 2: we see its back, its right side and the top of its head from behind; its face is hidden. It is foreshortened as seen from above: the top of the head, the shoulders or back and the upper body are large, the legs short.

Light: outdoor daylight, exactly as in Image 2; the figure stays as dark and as muted as in Image 2, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top and the upper-left side with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows. Nothing glows more than it does in Image 2. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, exactly the hand of Image 2; a muted earthy palette with its own colours exactly as Image 2 shows them; soft painterly edges, small crisp highlights and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges. A strong, simple, readable silhouette in every pose. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The giant: an old mountain giant, four men tall, a giant and not a man: coarse, heavy, massive features, a neck as thick as the head; a huge broad brutish face with a heavy jutting brow, small deep-set pale eyes and a heavy sullen scowl; weathered grey-tan skin rough as granite with pale lichen-grey patches; a bald head with a few long grey wisps; a matted grey beard; a cloak of stitched goat and bear hides over the shoulders and back, pulled up high around the neck; a rope of knotted hide across the chest; bare heavy arms and legs wrapped in hide; a huge crude wooden club as long as a man, held in the right hand. Its marks, every one painted clearly: the bald head with a few long grey wisps; small stones and bone beads knotted into the matted grey beard; a necklace of huge animal teeth; the cloak of stitched goat and bear hides; the broken, flattened nose. Seen from behind and above, the bald head with its grey wisps, the hide cloak over the back and shoulders and the club show clearly; the beard shows at the sides of the head.
Proportions: a giant's body, massive and heavy, with long thick arms and huge hands; the head about one sixth of the standing height; not a dwarf, not a big-headed figure.

Size: in each cell the figure fills the cell exactly as its maquette does in Image 1 and stands in the same place, with clean background all round it; nothing is cropped and no part of one figure reaches into a neighbouring cell.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No pink, magenta, violet or purple anywhere on the figure.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, dividing lines between the cells, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; fire, flames, breath, smoke, sparks, floating embers, magic light or mist (the game draws every effect).
